No pending dependency is named exactly when the item is ready.

∀σ,x:depAt⁡(σ,x)=⊥  ⟺  ready(σ,x)\displaystyle \forall \sigma, x:\quad \operatorname{depAt}(\sigma, x) = \bot \iff \mathrm{ready}(\sigma, x)
Admit.writeAt_nonetheoremagreel.320

No write conflict is named exactly when every running item is related or has no write conflict.

∀σ,x:wAt⁡(σ,x)=⊥  ⟺  ∀y∈Run: x∼y ∨ ¬(x⋈y)\displaystyle \forall \sigma, x:\quad \operatorname{wAt}(\sigma, x) = \bot \iff \forall y \in \mathit{Run}:\ x \sim y \ \lor\ \lnot(x \bowtie y)
Admit.devAt_nonetheoremagreel.332

No busy device is named exactly when every running item is related or shares no device.

∀σ,x:vAt⁡(σ,x)=⊥  ⟺  ∀y∈Run: x∼y ∨ V(x)∩V(y)=∅\displaystyle \forall \sigma, x:\quad \operatorname{vAt}(\sigma, x) = \bot \iff \forall y \in \mathit{Run}:\ x \sim y \ \lor\ V(x) \cap V(y) = \emptyset
Admit.budgetAt_nonetheoremagreel.344

No overflowing resource is named exactly when the item fits.

∀B,σ,x:bAt⁡(B,σ,x)=⊥  ⟺  fits(B,σ,x)\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, x:\quad \operatorname{bAt}(B, \sigma, x) = \bot \iff \mathrm{fits}(B, \sigma, x)
Admit.heldAt_nonetheoremagreel.351

No holding item is named exactly when the item is not held.

∀B,σ,x:hAt⁡(B,σ,x)=⊥  ⟺  ¬held(B,σ,x)\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, x:\quad \operatorname{hAt}(B, \sigma, x) = \bot \iff \lnot\mathrm{held}(B, \sigma, x)
Admit.free_ifftheoremagreel.358

Free, unfolded: every unrelated running item has no write conflict and shares no device.

∀σ,x:free(σ,x)  ⟺  ∀y∈Run: ¬(x∼y)⇒¬(x⋈y)∧V(x)∩V(y)=∅\displaystyle \forall \sigma, x:\quad \mathrm{free}(\sigma, x) \iff \forall y \in \mathit{Run}:\ \lnot(x \sim y) \Rightarrow \lnot(x \bowtie y) \land V(x) \cap V(y) = \emptyset
Admit.admit_eq_admittheoremagreel.368

The decision is admit exactly when none of the six checks names anything.

∀B,σ,x:admit⁡(B,σ,x)=admit  ⟺  nfAt⁡(B,x)=depAt⁡(σ,x)=wAt⁡(σ,x)=vAt⁡(σ,x)=bAt⁡(B,σ,x)=hAt⁡(B,σ,x)=⊥\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, x:\quad \operatorname{admit}(B, \sigma, x) = \mathrm{admit} \iff \operatorname{nfAt}(B, x) = \operatorname{depAt}(\sigma, x) = \operatorname{wAt}(\sigma, x) = \operatorname{vAt}(\sigma, x) = \operatorname{bAt}(B, \sigma, x) = \operatorname{hAt}(B, \sigma, x) = \bot
Admit.fits_not_unfittheoremagreel.389

An item that fits next to the running items fits the whole budget.

∀B,σ,x:fits(B,σ,x)⇒¬unfit(B,x)\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, x:\quad \mathrm{fits}(B, \sigma, x) \Rightarrow \lnot\mathrm{unfit}(B, x)
Admit.admit_ifftheoremagreel.398

**The decision is admit exactly when** the item is ready, free, fits, and not held (the neverFits check is implied by fits).

∀B,σ,x:admit⁡(B,σ,x)=admit  ⟺  ready(σ,x)∧free(σ,x)∧fits(B,σ,x)∧¬held(B,σ,x)\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, x:\quad \operatorname{admit}(B, \sigma, x) = \mathrm{admit} \iff \mathrm{ready}(\sigma, x) \land \mathrm{free}(\sigma, x) \land \mathrm{fits}(B, \sigma, x) \land \lnot\mathrm{held}(B, \sigma, x)
Admit.unfit_reportedtheoremagreel.428

**An item that never fits is named at once**: the decision is neverFits for some resource, never a silent wait.

∀B,σ,x:unfit(B,x)  ⇒  ∃r∈R: admit⁡(B,σ,x)=queue(neverFits(r))∧d(x)(r)>B(r)\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, x:\quad \mathrm{unfit}(B, x) \;\Rightarrow\; \exists r \in \mathcal R:\ \operatorname{admit}(B, \sigma, x) = \mathrm{queue}(\mathrm{neverFits}(r)) \land d(x)(r) > B(r)
Admit.pickFrom_memtheoremagreel.460

The fold returns its seed or one of the items it scanned.

∀t,b,ks:pickFrom⁡t(b,ks)=b ∨ pickFrom⁡t(b,ks)∈ks\displaystyle \forall t, b, ks:\quad \operatorname{pickFrom}_t(b, ks) = b \ \lor\ \operatorname{pickFrom}_t(b, ks) \in ks
Admit.pick_memtheoremagreel.474

pick returns a member of the list.

∀t,Q,j:pick⁡t(Q)=j⇒j∈Q\displaystyle \forall t, Q, j:\quad \operatorname{pick}_t(Q) = j \Rightarrow j \in Q
Admit.eq_of_nodup_maptheoremagreel.574

If the image list of l under f has no repeats, two members of l with the same image are equal.

∀f,l,a,b:[ f(c)∣c∈l ] has no repeats ∧ a,b∈l ∧ f(a)=f(b)⇒a=b\displaystyle \forall f, l, a, b:\quad [\, f(c) \mid c \in l \,] \text{ has no repeats} \ \land\ a, b \in l \ \land\ f(a) = f(b) \Rightarrow a = b
Admit.wconf_commtheoremagreel.590

Write conflict is symmetric.

∀x,y:x⋈y  ⟺  y⋈x\displaystyle \forall x, y:\quad x \bowtie y \iff y \bowtie x
Admit.devShare_commtheoremagreel.602

Device overlap is symmetric.

∀x,y:V(x)∩V(y)≠∅  ⟺  V(y)∩V(x)≠∅\displaystyle \forall x, y:\quad V(x) \cap V(y) \ne \emptyset \iff V(y) \cap V(x) \ne \emptyset
Admit.related_commtheoremagreel.613

Relatedness is symmetric.

∀x,y:x∼y  ⟺  y∼x\displaystyle \forall x, y:\quad x \sim y \iff y \sim x
Admit.used_filter_letheoremagreel.620

The summed demand of a filtered list is at most that of the list.

∀p,l,r:used⁡([ y∈l∣p(y) ],r)≤used⁡(l,r)\displaystyle \forall p, l, r:\quad \operatorname{used}([\, y \in l \mid p(y) \,], r) \le \operatorname{used}(l, r)
Admit.chosen_soundtheoremagreel.631

chosen returns a queued item whose decision is admit.

∀B,σ,x:chosen⁡(B,σ)=x⇒x∈Q∧admit⁡(B,σ,x)=admit\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, x:\quad \operatorname{chosen}(B, \sigma) = x \Rightarrow x \in Q \land \operatorname{admit}(B, \sigma, x) = \mathrm{admit}
Admit.admit_conservingtheoremagreel.641

**Work conservation.** If some queued item would be admitted, admitStep admits something.

∀B,σ,x:x∈Q∧admit⁡(B,σ,x)=admit⇒chosen⁡(B,σ)≠⊥\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, x:\quad x \in Q \land \operatorname{admit}(B, \sigma, x) = \mathrm{admit} \Rightarrow \operatorname{chosen}(B, \sigma) \ne \bot
Admit.nodup_map_sublisttheoremagreel.653

Nodup of an image survives taking a sublist.

∀f,l′,l:l′ a sublist of l ∧ [ f(a)∣a∈l ] has no repeats⇒[ f(a)∣a∈l′ ] has no repeats\displaystyle \forall f, l', l:\quad l' \text{ a sublist of } l \ \land\ [\, f(a) \mid a \in l \,] \text{ has no repeats} \Rightarrow [\, f(a) \mid a \in l' \,] \text{ has no repeats}
Admit.nodup_admittheoremagreel.661

Admitting x from Q keeps the image list free of repeats (the admitted copy keeps its image).

∀f,R,Q,x,x′:x∈Q∧f(x′)=f(x)∧[ f(y)∣y∈R+ ⁣ ⁣+Q ] has no repeats⇒[ f(y)∣y∈x′::R+ ⁣ ⁣+[ y∈Q∣id(y)≠id(x) ] ] has no repeats\displaystyle \forall f, R, Q, x, x':\quad x \in Q \land f(x') = f(x) \land [\, f(y) \mid y \in R \mathbin{+\!\!+} Q \,] \text{ has no repeats} \Rightarrow [\, f(y) \mid y \in x' :: R \mathbin{+\!\!+} [\, y \in Q \mid \mathit{id}(y) \ne \mathit{id}(x) \,] \,] \text{ has no repeats}
Admit.inv_steptheoremagreel.688

**The invariant is preserved by every command.**

∀B,σ,c:Inv(B,σ)⇒Inv(B,step⁡(B,σ,c))\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, c:\quad \mathrm{Inv}(B, \sigma) \Rightarrow \mathrm{Inv}(B, \operatorname{step}(B, \sigma, c))
Admit.inv_inittheoremagreel.799

The empty state satisfies the invariant.

∀B:Inv(B,σ0)\displaystyle \forall B:\quad \mathrm{Inv}(B, \sigma_0)
Admit.inv_reachabletheoremagreel.807

Every reachable state satisfies the invariant.

∀B,σ:ReachB(σ)⇒Inv(B,σ)\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma:\quad \mathrm{Reach}_B(\sigma) \Rightarrow \mathrm{Inv}(B, \sigma)
Admit.writes_disjointtheoremagreel.816

**No two unrelated running items write the same file** (in every reachable state).

∀B,σ:ReachB(σ)⇒∀x,y∈Run: x≠y∧¬(x∼y)⇒¬(x⋈y)\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma:\quad \mathrm{Reach}_B(\sigma) \Rightarrow \forall x, y \in \mathit{Run}:\ x \ne y \land \lnot(x \sim y) \Rightarrow \lnot(x \bowtie y)
Admit.devices_exclusivetheoremagreel.827

**Devices are exclusive between unrelated running items** (in every reachable state).

∀B,σ:ReachB(σ)⇒∀x,y∈Run: x≠y∧¬(x∼y)⇒V(x)∩V(y)=∅\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma:\quad \mathrm{Reach}_B(\sigma) \Rightarrow \forall x, y \in \mathit{Run}:\ x \ne y \land \lnot(x \sim y) \Rightarrow V(x) \cap V(y) = \emptyset
Admit.deps_respectedtheoremagreel.838

**Dependencies are respected**: every running item's dependencies have landed (in every reachable state).

∀B,σ:ReachB(σ)⇒∀x∈Run, ∀e∈D(x): e∈Done\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma:\quad \mathrm{Reach}_B(\sigma) \Rightarrow \forall x \in \mathit{Run},\ \forall e \in D(x):\ e \in \mathit{Done}
Admit.done_growstheoremagreel.850

**Done only grows**: no command removes a landed id.

∀B,σ,c:∀e∈Done(σ): e∈Done(step⁡(B,σ,c))\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, c:\quad \forall e \in \mathit{Done}(\sigma):\ e \in \mathit{Done}(\operatorname{step}(B, \sigma, c))
Admit.within_budgettheoremagreel.862

**The budget holds** in every reachable state.

∀B,σ:ReachB(σ)⇒∀r∈R: ∑x∈Rund(x)(r)≤B(r)\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma:\quad \mathrm{Reach}_B(\sigma) \Rightarrow \forall r \in \mathcal R:\ \sum_{x \in \mathit{Run}} d(x)(r) \le B(r)
Admit.aged_not_overtakentheoremagreel.869

**An aged item is never overtaken by a competitor.** If z is queued, aged, ready, not unfit and goes before x, and admitStep admits x (with a different id), then z does not compete with x.

∀B,σ,z,x:z∈Q, aged(t,z), ready(σ,z), ¬unfit(B,z), before⁡t(z,x), id(z)≠id(x), chosen⁡(B,σ)=x  ⇒  ¬comp(B,σ,z,x)\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, z, x:\quad z \in Q,\ \mathrm{aged}(t, z),\ \mathrm{ready}(\sigma, z),\ \lnot\mathrm{unfit}(B, z),\ \operatorname{before}_t(z, x),\ \mathit{id}(z) \ne \mathit{id}(x),\ \operatorname{chosen}(B, \sigma) = x \;\Rightarrow\; \lnot\mathrm{comp}(B, \sigma, z, x)
Admit.Steps.transtheoremagreel.933

Micro-step sequences compose.

∀B,σ,τ,υ:StepsB(σ,τ)∧StepsB(τ,υ)⇒StepsB(σ,υ)\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, \tau, \upsilon:\quad \mathrm{Steps}_B(\sigma, \tau) \land \mathrm{Steps}_B(\tau, \upsilon) \Rightarrow \mathrm{Steps}_B(\sigma, \upsilon)
Admit.steps_admitNtheoremagreel.943

admitN is a sequence of admit commands.

∀B,n,σ:StepsB(σ,admitN⁡(B,n,σ))\displaystyle \forall B, n, \sigma:\quad \mathrm{Steps}_B(\sigma, \operatorname{admitN}(B, n, \sigma))
Admit.steps_eventtheoremagreel.955

An event is a sequence of commands.

∀B,σ,c:StepsB(σ,event⁡(B,σ,c))\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, c:\quad \mathrm{Steps}_B(\sigma, \operatorname{event}(B, \sigma, c))
Admit.admitStep_shrinkstheoremagreel.962

Admitting removes the admitted item from the queue, so the queue shrinks.

∀B,σ,x:chosen⁡(B,σ)=x⇒∣Q(admitStep⁡(B,σ))∣<∣Q(σ)∣\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, x:\quad \operatorname{chosen}(B, \sigma) = x \Rightarrow |Q(\operatorname{admitStep}(B, \sigma))| < |Q(\sigma)|
Admit.chosen_admitNtheoremagreel.972

After at least |Q| admit steps nothing is admissible.

∀B,n,σ:∣Q(σ)∣≤n⇒chosen⁡(B,admitN⁡(B,n,σ))=⊥\displaystyle \forall B, n, \sigma:\quad |Q(\sigma)| \le n \Rightarrow \operatorname{chosen}(B, \operatorname{admitN}(B, n, \sigma)) = \bot
Admit.chosen_eventtheoremagreel.989

Every event ends quiescent: nothing queued is admissible.

∀B,σ,c:chosen⁡(B,event⁡(B,σ,c))=⊥\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, c:\quad \operatorname{chosen}(B, \operatorname{event}(B, \sigma, c)) = \bot
Admit.len_filter_monotheoremagreel.1025

Filtering by a weaker predicate keeps at least as many items.

∀l,p,q:(∀a∈l: p(a)⇒q(a))⇒∣[ a∈l∣p(a) ]∣≤∣[ a∈l∣q(a) ]∣\displaystyle \forall l, p, q:\quad (\forall a \in l:\ p(a) \Rightarrow q(a)) \Rightarrow |[\, a \in l \mid p(a) \,]| \le |[\, a \in l \mid q(a) \,]|
Admit.len_filter_lttheoremagreel.1042

... and strictly fewer when some item satisfies only the weaker predicate.

∀l,p,q:(∀a∈l: p(a)⇒q(a))∧(∃a∈l: q(a)∧¬p(a))⇒∣[ a∈l∣p(a) ]∣<∣[ a∈l∣q(a) ]∣\displaystyle \forall l, p, q:\quad (\forall a \in l:\ p(a) \Rightarrow q(a)) \land (\exists a \in l:\ q(a) \land \lnot p(a)) \Rightarrow |[\, a \in l \mid p(a) \,]| < |[\, a \in l \mid q(a) \,]|
Admit.used_sublisttheoremagreel.1064

Demand summed over a sublist is at most the sum over the list.

∀l′,l,r:l′ a sublist of l⇒used⁡(l′,r)≤used⁡(l,r)\displaystyle \forall l', l, r:\quad l' \text{ a sublist of } l \Rightarrow \operatorname{used}(l', r) \le \operatorname{used}(l, r)
Admit.le_of_not_unfittheoremagreel.1074

An item that is not unfit fits in the empty machine.

∀B,x:¬unfit(B,x)⇒∀r∈R: d(x)(r)≤B(r)\displaystyle \forall B, x:\quad \lnot\mathrm{unfit}(B, x) \Rightarrow \forall r \in \mathcal R:\ d(x)(r) \le B(r)
Admit.eff_agedtheoremagreel.1082

Aged items have effective priority 0.

∀t,z:aged(t,z)⇒eff⁡t(z)=0\displaystyle \forall t, z:\quad \mathrm{aged}(t, z) \Rightarrow \operatorname{eff}_t(z) = 0
Admit.before_of_agedtheoremagreel.1094

An aged item goes before every item with a larger or equal arrival number.

∀t,e,x:aged(t,e)∧seq(e)≤seq(x)⇒before⁡t(e,x)\displaystyle \forall t, e, x:\quad \mathrm{aged}(t, e) \land \mathit{seq}(e) \le \mathit{seq}(x) \Rightarrow \operatorname{before}_t(e, x)
Admit.seq_le_of_beforetheoremagreel.1105

Between two aged items, before is arrival order.

∀t,a,b:aged(t,a)∧aged(t,b)∧before⁡t(a,b)⇒seq(a)≤seq(b)\displaystyle \forall t, a, b:\quad \mathrm{aged}(t, a) \land \mathrm{aged}(t, b) \land \operatorname{before}_t(a, b) \Rightarrow \mathit{seq}(a) \le \mathit{seq}(b)
Admit.aged_monotheoremagreel.1117

Aging is monotone in time.

∀t,t′,z:aged(t,z)∧t≤t′⇒aged(t′,z)\displaystyle \forall t, t', z:\quad \mathrm{aged}(t, z) \land t \le t' \Rightarrow \mathrm{aged}(t', z)
Admit.ready_monotheoremagreel.1124

Readiness is monotone in the landed set.

∀σ,σ′,x:Done(σ)⊆Done(σ′)∧ready(σ,x)⇒ready(σ′,x)\displaystyle \forall \sigma, \sigma', x:\quad \mathit{Done}(\sigma) \subseteq \mathit{Done}(\sigma') \land \mathrm{ready}(\sigma, x) \Rightarrow \mathrm{ready}(\sigma', x)
Admit.elig_monotheoremagreel.1133

Eligibility is monotone in time and in the landed set.

∀σ,σ′,o:t(σ)≤t(σ′)∧Done(σ)⊆Done(σ′)∧elig⁡(σ,o)⇒elig⁡(σ′,o)\displaystyle \forall \sigma, \sigma', o:\quad t(\sigma) \le t(\sigma') \land \mathit{Done}(\sigma) \subseteq \mathit{Done}(\sigma') \land \operatorname{elig}(\sigma, o) \Rightarrow \operatorname{elig}(\sigma', o)
Admit.t_steptheoremagreel.1142

The clock never runs backwards.

∀B,σ,c:t(σ)≤t(step⁡(B,σ,c))\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, c:\quad t(\sigma) \le t(\operatorname{step}(B, \sigma, c))
Admit.next_steptheoremagreel.1153

next never decreases.

∀B,σ,c:next(σ)≤next(step⁡(B,σ,c))\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, c:\quad \mathit{next}(\sigma) \le \mathit{next}(\operatorname{step}(B, \sigma, c))
Admit.queue_steptheoremagreel.1164

Every item queued after a step was queued before, or is the newly enqueued item numbered next.

∀B,σ,c,y:y∈Q(step⁡(B,σ,c))⇒y∈Q(σ)∨seq(y)=next(σ)\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, c, y:\quad y \in Q(\operatorname{step}(B, \sigma, c)) \Rightarrow y \in Q(\sigma) \lor \mathit{seq}(y) = \mathit{next}(\sigma)
Admit.gone_stepstheoremagreel.1192

Once gone, z stays gone along micro steps.

∀B,z,σ,τ:StepsB(σ,τ)∧gone⁡(z,σ)⇒gone⁡(z,τ)\displaystyle \forall B, z, \sigma, \tau:\quad \mathrm{Steps}_B(\sigma, \tau) \land \operatorname{gone}(z, \sigma) \Rightarrow \operatorname{gone}(z, \tau)
Admit.gone_tracetheoremagreel.1207

Once gone, z stays gone along a trace.

∀B,d,z,σ,τ:TraceB,d(σ,τ)∧gone⁡(z,σ)⇒gone⁡(z,τ)\displaystyle \forall B, d, z, \sigma, \tau:\quad \mathrm{Trace}_{B,d}(\sigma, \tau) \land \operatorname{gone}(z, \sigma) \Rightarrow \operatorname{gone}(z, \tau)
Admit.eq_of_seqtheoremagreel.1243

Two queued items with the same arrival number are equal (given the invariant).

∀B,σ,a,b:Inv(B,σ)∧a,b∈Q∧seq(a)=seq(b)⇒a=b\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, a, b:\quad \mathrm{Inv}(B, \sigma) \land a, b \in Q \land \mathit{seq}(a) = \mathit{seq}(b) \Rightarrow a = b
Admit.eq_of_idtheoremagreel.1251

Two queued items with the same id are equal (given the invariant).

∀B,σ,a,b:Inv(B,σ)∧a,b∈Q∧id(a)=id(b)⇒a=b\displaystyle \forall B, \sigma, a, b:\quad \mathrm{Inv}(B, \sigma) \land a, b \in Q \land \mathit{id}(a) = \mathit{id}(b) \Rightarrow a = b
Admit.elig_of_seq_eqtheoremagreel.1259

A queued item numbered like z is eligible (from the frame).

∀B,z,G,t0,σ,e:Base(B,z,G,t0,σ)∧e∈Q∧seq(e)=seq(z)⇒elig⁡(σ,e)\displaystyle \forall B, z, G, t_0, \sigma, e:\quad \mathrm{Base}(B, z, G, t_0, \sigma) \land e \in Q \land \mathit{seq}(e) = \mathit{seq}(z) \Rightarrow \operatorname{elig}(\sigma, e)
Admit.base_steptheoremagreel.1269

The frame is preserved by every command.

∀B,z,G,t0,σ,c:Base(B,z,G,t0,σ)⇒Base(B,z,G,t0,step⁡(B,σ,c))\displaystyle \forall B, z, G, t_0, \sigma, c:\quad \mathrm{Base}(B, z, G, t_0, \sigma) \Rightarrow \mathrm{Base}(B, z, G, t_0, \operatorname{step}(B, \sigma, c))
Admit.base_stepstheoremagreel.1329

The frame is preserved along micro steps.

∀B,z,G,t0,σ,τ:StepsB(σ,τ)∧Base(B,z,G,t0,σ)⇒Base(B,z,G,t0,τ)\displaystyle \forall B, z, G, t_0, \sigma, \tau:\quad \mathrm{Steps}_B(\sigma, \tau) \land \mathrm{Base}(B, z, G, t_0, \sigma) \Rightarrow \mathrm{Base}(B, z, G, t_0, \tau)
Admit.psi_eligtheoremagreel.1339

When the queue is unchanged and eligibility only grows, the measure does not grow, and it stays equal only if no older possible competitor became eligible.

∀B,z,σ,σ′:Q(σ′)=Q(σ)∧(∀o: elig⁡(σ,o)⇒elig⁡(σ′,o))⇒Ψ(σ′)≤Ψ(σ)∧(Ψ(σ′)=Ψ(σ)⇒∀o∈Q: oldOk⁡(B,z,o)∧elig⁡(σ′,o)⇒elig⁡(σ,o))\displaystyle \forall B, z, \sigma, \sigma':\quad Q(\sigma') = Q(\sigma) \land (\forall o:\ \operatorname{elig}(\sigma, o) \Rightarrow \operatorname{elig}(\sigma', o)) \Rightarrow \Psi(\sigma') \le \Psi(\sigma) \land \big(\Psi(\sigma') = \Psi(\sigma) \Rightarrow \forall o \in Q:\ \operatorname{oldOk}(B, z, o) \land \operatorname{elig}(\sigma', o) \Rightarrow \operatorname{elig}(\sigma, o)\big)
Admit.psi_admittheoremagreel.1362

Admitting x does not grow the measure, and strictly shrinks it when x is an older possible competitor.

∀B,z,σ,x:chosen⁡(B,σ)=x⇒Ψ(admitStep⁡(B,σ))≤Ψ(σ)∧(oldOk⁡(B,z,x)⇒Ψ(admitStep⁡(B,σ))<Ψ(σ))\displaystyle \forall B, z, \sigma, x:\quad \operatorname{chosen}(B, \sigma) = x \Rightarrow \Psi(\operatorname{admitStep}(B, \sigma)) \le \Psi(\sigma) \land \big(\operatorname{oldOk}(B, z, x) \Rightarrow \Psi(\operatorname{admitStep}(B, \sigma)) < \Psi(\sigma)\big)
Admit.psi_steptheoremagreel.1387

The measure never grows under a command.

∀B,z,G,t0,σ,c:Base(B,z,G,t0,σ)⇒Ψ(step⁡(B,σ,c))≤Ψ(σ)\displaystyle \forall B, z, G, t_0, \sigma, c:\quad \mathrm{Base}(B, z, G, t_0, \sigma) \Rightarrow \Psi(\operatorname{step}(B, \sigma, c)) \le \Psi(\sigma)
Admit.ghost_steptheoremagreel.1414

The ghost invariant survives every command that leaves the measure unchanged.

∀B,z,G,t0,σ,c:Base(B,z,G,t0,σ)∧Ghost(B,z,G,σ)∧Ψ(step⁡(B,σ,c))=Ψ(σ)⇒Ghost(B,z,G,step⁡(B,σ,c))\displaystyle \forall B, z, G, t_0, \sigma, c:\quad \mathrm{Base}(B, z, G, t_0, \sigma) \land \mathrm{Ghost}(B, z, G, \sigma) \land \Psi(\operatorname{step}(B, \sigma, c)) = \Psi(\sigma) \Rightarrow \mathrm{Ghost}(B, z, G, \operatorname{step}(B, \sigma, c))
Admit.ghost_stepstheoremagreel.1508

Along micro steps the measure never grows, and the ghost invariant survives if the measure is unchanged.

∀B,z,G,t0,σ,τ:StepsB(σ,τ)∧Base(B,z,G,t0,σ)⇒Ψ(τ)≤Ψ(σ)∧(Ghost(B,z,G,σ)∧Ψ(τ)=Ψ(σ)⇒Ghost(B,z,G,τ))\displaystyle \forall B, z, G, t_0, \sigma, \tau:\quad \mathrm{Steps}_B(\sigma, \tau) \land \mathrm{Base}(B, z, G, t_0, \sigma) \Rightarrow \Psi(\tau) \le \Psi(\sigma) \land \big(\mathrm{Ghost}(B, z, G, \sigma) \land \Psi(\tau) = \Psi(\sigma) \Rightarrow \mathrm{Ghost}(B, z, G, \tau)\big)
Admit.stuck_falsetheoremagreel.1524

**The stuck state is impossible.** In a quiescent state where the frame and the ghost invariant hold, no item started before the beginning still runs, and z is queued, the least-numbered qualified item would be admissible.

∀B,z,G,t0,σ:Base∧Ghost∧chosen⁡(B,σ)=⊥∧(∀y∈Run: seq(y)∉G)∧z∈Q∧¬unfit(B,z)⇒⊥\displaystyle \forall B, z, G, t_0, \sigma:\quad \mathrm{Base} \land \mathrm{Ghost} \land \operatorname{chosen}(B, \sigma) = \bot \land (\forall y \in \mathit{Run}:\ \mathit{seq}(y) \notin G) \land z \in Q \land \lnot\mathrm{unfit}(B, z) \Rightarrow \bot
Admit.phasetheoremagreel.1567

**One phase of the liveness argument.** Starting in a quiescent state inside the frame with measure k, time before t0 + dmax and the ghost invariant, a trace that still has z queued at its end either ends before t0 + dmax, or passes a quiescent state, before t0 + dmax, where the measure has dropped below k.

∀B,d,z,G,t0,k,σ,σj:TraceB,d(σ,σj)∧Base(σ)∧Ghost(σ)∧Ψ(σ)=k∧chosen⁡(B,σ)=⊥∧t(σ)<t0+d∧¬unfit(B,z)∧z∈Q(σj)⇒t(σj)<t0+d∨∃σa: TraceB,d(σa,σj)∧Base(σa)∧chosen⁡(B,σa)=⊥∧Ψ(σa)<k∧t(σa)<t0+d\displaystyle \forall B, d, z, G, t_0, k, \sigma, \sigma_j:\quad \mathrm{Trace}_{B,d}(\sigma, \sigma_j) \land \mathrm{Base}(\sigma) \land \mathrm{Ghost}(\sigma) \land \Psi(\sigma) = k \land \operatorname{chosen}(B, \sigma) = \bot \land t(\sigma) < t_0 + d \land \lnot\mathrm{unfit}(B, z) \land z \in Q(\sigma_j) \Rightarrow t(\sigma_j) < t_0 + d \lor \exists \sigma_a:\ \mathrm{Trace}_{B,d}(\sigma_a, \sigma_j) \land \mathrm{Base}(\sigma_a) \land \operatorname{chosen}(B, \sigma_a) = \bot \land \Psi(\sigma_a) < k \land t(\sigma_a) < t_0 + d
Admit.aged_admitted_bytheoremagreel.1603

**An aged job is admitted in bounded time** (restated aged_admitted_by). Take a quiescent state satisfying the invariant in which z is queued, aged, ready and can ever fit. Along any trace where every running job ends before start + dmax (with dmax > 0), every later state that still has z queued has clock below t + (1 + \Psi) \cdot dmax, where \Psi counts the queued older items that can ever fit, twice for those not yet eligible.

∀B,d,σi,σj,z:d>0∧Inv(B,σi)∧chosen⁡(B,σi)=⊥∧z∈Q(σi)∧aged(t(σi),z)∧ready(σi,z)∧¬unfit(B,z)∧TraceB,d(σi,σj)∧z∈Q(σj)⇒t(σj)<t(σi)+(1+ΨB,z(σi))⋅d\displaystyle \forall B, d, \sigma_i, \sigma_j, z:\quad d > 0 \land \mathrm{Inv}(B, \sigma_i) \land \operatorname{chosen}(B, \sigma_i) = \bot \land z \in Q(\sigma_i) \land \mathrm{aged}(t(\sigma_i), z) \land \mathrm{ready}(\sigma_i, z) \land \lnot\mathrm{unfit}(B, z) \land \mathrm{Trace}_{B,d}(\sigma_i, \sigma_j) \land z \in Q(\sigma_j) \Rightarrow t(\sigma_j) < t(\sigma_i) + (1 + \Psi_{B,z}(\sigma_i)) \cdot d
Admit.okTrace_soundtheoremagreel.1673

A checked command list is a trace.

∀B,d,cs,σ:ok⁡(B,d,σ,cs)⇒TraceB,d(σ,run⁡(B,σ,cs))\displaystyle \forall B, d, cs, \sigma:\quad \operatorname{ok}(B, d, \sigma, cs) \Rightarrow \mathrm{Trace}_{B,d}(\sigma, \operatorname{run}(B, \sigma, cs))

An item: a workstream or a heavy job. x=(id, parent, W(x), D(x), d(x), V(x), seq, enq, base, start)∈String×String⊥×String∗×String∗×NR×V∗×N4\displaystyle x = (\mathit{id},\ \mathit{parent},\ W(x),\ D(x),\ d(x),\ V(x),\ \mathit{seq},\ \mathit{enq},\ \mathit{base},\ \mathit{start}) \in \mathrm{String} \times \mathrm{String}_\bot \times \mathrm{String}^{*} \times \mathrm{String}^{*} \times \mathbb N^{\mathcal R} \times \mathcal V^{*} \times \mathbb N^{4}

Admit.admitdefagreel.280

The admission rule: the first failing check, in this order, gives the reason; otherwise admit.

admit⁡(B,σ,x)={queue(neverFits(r))nfAt⁡(B,x)=rqueue(depPending(e))else if depAt⁡(σ,x)=equeue(writeConflict(p,y))else if wAt⁡(σ,x)=(p,y)queue(deviceBusy(v,y))else if vAt⁡(σ,x)=(v,y)queue(overBudget(r,d(x)(r),B(r)−˙used⁡(Run,r)))else if bAt⁡(B,σ,x)=rqueue(behindAged(id(z)))else if hAt⁡(B,σ,x)=zadmitotherwise\displaystyle \operatorname{admit}(B, \sigma, x) = \begin{cases} \mathrm{queue}(\mathrm{neverFits}(r)) & \operatorname{nfAt}(B, x) = r \\ \mathrm{queue}(\mathrm{depPending}(e)) & \text{else if } \operatorname{depAt}(\sigma, x) = e \\ \mathrm{queue}(\mathrm{writeConflict}(p, y)) & \text{else if } \operatorname{wAt}(\sigma, x) = (p, y) \\ \mathrm{queue}(\mathrm{deviceBusy}(v, y)) & \text{else if } \operatorname{vAt}(\sigma, x) = (v, y) \\ \mathrm{queue}(\mathrm{overBudget}(r, d(x)(r), B(r) \mathbin{\dot-} \operatorname{used}(\mathit{Run}, r))) & \text{else if } \operatorname{bAt}(B, \sigma, x) = r \\ \mathrm{queue}(\mathrm{behindAged}(\mathit{id}(z))) & \text{else if } \operatorname{hAt}(B, \sigma, x) = z \\ \mathrm{admit} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

Admit.finishdefagreel.504

An item ends: it leaves Run; its id joins Done when it landed and was running.

Admit.Invinductiveagreel.558

The invariant: ids and arrival numbers are unique over Run and Q, arrival numbers are below next, running items started no later than now, unrelated running items have no write conflict and share no device, running items are ready, and the budget holds.

Inv(B,σ)  ⟺  [t][ id(x)∣x∈Run+ ⁣ ⁣+Q ] and [ seq(x)∣x∈Run+ ⁣ ⁣+Q ] have no repeats, ∀x∈Run+ ⁣ ⁣+Q: seq(x)<next,  ∀x∈Run: start(x)≤t∧ready(σ,x),∀x,y∈Run, id(x)≠id(y), ¬(x∼y): ¬(x⋈y)∧V(x)∩V(y)=∅,  ∀r∈R: ∑x∈Rund(x)(r)≤B(r)\displaystyle \mathrm{Inv}(B, \sigma) \iff \begin{aligned}[t] & [\, \mathit{id}(x) \mid x \in \mathit{Run} \mathbin{+\!\!+} Q \,] \text{ and } [\, \mathit{seq}(x) \mid x \in \mathit{Run} \mathbin{+\!\!+} Q \,] \text{ have no repeats},\ \forall x \in \mathit{Run} \mathbin{+\!\!+} Q:\ \mathit{seq}(x) < \mathit{next},\ \ \forall x \in \mathit{Run}:\ \mathit{start}(x) \le t \land \mathrm{ready}(\sigma, x), \\ & \forall x, y \in \mathit{Run},\ \mathit{id}(x) \ne \mathit{id}(y),\ \lnot(x \sim y):\ \lnot(x \bowtie y) \land V(x) \cap V(y) = \emptyset,\ \ \forall r \in \mathcal R:\ \textstyle\sum_{x \in \mathit{Run}} d(x)(r) \le B(r) \end{aligned}

At most n admit steps, stopping early when nothing is admissible.

Admit.admitAlldefagreel.902

Admit until quiescent (|Q| steps always suffice).

Admit.eventdefagreel.908

One trace event: apply a command, then admit until quiescent.

event⁡(B,σ,c)=admitAll⁡(B,step⁡(B,σ,c))\displaystyle \operatorname{event}(B, \sigma, c) = \operatorname{admitAll}(B, \operatorname{step}(B, \sigma, c))
Admit.Traceinductiveagreel.914

A trace of events in which every running item ends before start + dmax: an event may only move the clock to a time before the deadline of every item running before it.

Admit.Stepsinductiveagreel.925

Finite sequences of single commands (the micro steps inside events).

Admit.oldOkdefagreel.998

o is an older item that can ever fit (an older possible competitor of z).

oldOk⁡(B,z,o)  ⟺  seq(o)<seq(z)∧¬unfit(B,o)\displaystyle \operatorname{oldOk}(B, z, o) \iff \mathit{seq}(o) < \mathit{seq}(z) \land \lnot\mathrm{unfit}(B, o)
Admit.eligdefagreel.1004

Eligible: aged and ready.

elig⁡(σ,o)  ⟺  aged(t,o)∧ready(σ,o)\displaystyle \operatorname{elig}(\sigma, o) \iff \mathrm{aged}(t, o) \land \mathrm{ready}(\sigma, o)
Admit.psidefagreel.1010

The liveness measure of z: queued older possible competitors, counted once more while they are not yet eligible.

ΨB,z(σ)=∣[ o∈Q∣oldOk⁡(B,z,o) ]∣+∣[ o∈Q∣oldOk⁡(B,z,o)∧¬elig⁡(σ,o) ]∣(list filters, repeats counted)\displaystyle \Psi_{B,z}(\sigma) = \big|[\, o \in Q \mid \operatorname{oldOk}(B, z, o) \,]\big| + \big|[\, o \in Q \mid \operatorname{oldOk}(B, z, o) \land \lnot\operatorname{elig}(\sigma, o) \,]\big| \quad (\text{list filters, repeats counted})
Admit.qualdefagreel.1018

Qualified items for the ghost invariant: no newer than z, can ever fit, and eligible.

qual⁡(B,z,σ,e)  ⟺  seq(e)≤seq(z)∧¬unfit(B,e)∧elig⁡(σ,e)\displaystyle \operatorname{qual}(B, z, \sigma, e) \iff \mathit{seq}(e) \le \mathit{seq}(z) \land \lnot\mathrm{unfit}(B, e) \land \operatorname{elig}(\sigma, e)
Admit.Gonedefagreel.1186

z has left the queue for good: its number is used and no queued item carries it.

gone⁡(z,σ)  ⟺  seq(z)<next∧∀y∈Q: seq(y)≠seq(z)\displaystyle \operatorname{gone}(z, \sigma) \iff \mathit{seq}(z) < \mathit{next} \land \forall y \in Q:\ \mathit{seq}(y) \ne \mathit{seq}(z)
Admit.Baseinductiveagreel.1217

The frame of the liveness argument, relative to z, the arrival numbers G of the items running at the start, and the start time t0.

Base(B,z,G,t0,σ)  ⟺  [t]Inv(B,σ)∧aged(t,z)∧ready(σ,z)∧seq(z)<next∧(∀g∈G: g<next)∧(∀y∈Q: seq(y)∉G)∧(∀y∈Run: seq(y)∈G⇒start(y)≤t0)∧(z∈Q∨∀y∈Q: seq(y)≠seq(z))\displaystyle \mathrm{Base}(B, z, G, t_0, \sigma) \iff \begin{aligned}[t] & \mathrm{Inv}(B, \sigma) \land \mathrm{aged}(t, z) \land \mathrm{ready}(\sigma, z) \land \mathit{seq}(z) < \mathit{next} \land \big(\forall g \in G:\ g < \mathit{next}\big) \\ & \land \big(\forall y \in Q:\ \mathit{seq}(y) \notin G\big) \land \big(\forall y \in \mathit{Run}:\ \mathit{seq}(y) \in G \Rightarrow \mathit{start}(y) \le t_0\big) \\ & \land \big(z \in Q \lor \forall y \in Q:\ \mathit{seq}(y) \ne \mathit{seq}(z)\big) \end{aligned}
Admit.Ghostinductiveagreel.1232

The ghost invariant: every qualified queued item is free of, and fits beside, the items started since the beginning (those whose number is not in G).

Ghost(B,z,G,σ)  ⟺  ∀e∈Q, qual⁡(B,z,σ,e): (∀y∈Run, seq(y)∉G: ¬(e⋈y)∧V(e)∩V(y)=∅)∧∀r∈R: d(e)(r)+∑y∈Run, seq(y)∉Gd(y)(r)≤B(r)\displaystyle \mathrm{Ghost}(B, z, G, \sigma) \iff \forall e \in Q,\ \operatorname{qual}(B, z, \sigma, e):\ \big(\forall y \in \mathit{Run},\ \mathit{seq}(y) \notin G:\ \lnot(e \bowtie y) \land V(e) \cap V(y) = \emptyset\big) \land \forall r \in \mathcal R:\ d(e)(r) + \textstyle\sum_{y \in \mathit{Run},\ \mathit{seq}(y) \notin G} d(y)(r) \le B(r)
Admit.runTracedefagreel.1655

Run a list of commands as events.

run⁡(B,σ,[ ])=σ,run⁡(B,σ,c::cs)=run⁡(B,event⁡(B,σ,c),cs)\displaystyle \operatorname{run}(B, \sigma, [\,]) = \sigma, \qquad \operatorname{run}(B, \sigma, c :: cs) = \operatorname{run}(B, \operatorname{event}(B, \sigma, c), cs)
Admit.okTracedefagreel.1663

Check the trace side condition for a list of commands: each event keeps the clock below the deadline of every item running before it.

ok⁡(B,d,σ,[ ]),ok⁡(B,d,σ,c::cs)  ⟺  (∀x∈Run(σ): t(event⁡(B,σ,c))<start(x)+d)∧ok⁡(B,d,event⁡(B,σ,c),cs)\displaystyle \operatorname{ok}(B, d, \sigma, [\,]), \qquad \operatorname{ok}(B, d, \sigma, c :: cs) \iff \big(\forall x \in \mathit{Run}(\sigma):\ t(\operatorname{event}(B, \sigma, c)) < \mathit{start}(x) + d\big) \land \operatorname{ok}(B, d, \operatorname{event}(B, \sigma, c), cs)

ParMetrics.sortS_sortedtheoremagreel.71

sortS sorts by start.

ParMetrics.mergeGo_starttheoremagreel.81

Every interval emitted by mergeGo starts no earlier than the current interval.

∀c,ys:ys sorted by s∧(∀y∈ys: sc≤sy)⇒∀o∈go⁡(c,ys): sc≤so\displaystyle \forall c, ys:\quad ys \text{ sorted by } s \land (\forall y \in ys:\ s_c \le s_y) \Rightarrow \forall o \in \operatorname{go}(c, ys):\ s_c \le s_o
ParMetrics.mergeGo_oktheoremagreel.98

mergeGo emits disjoint, separated, non-empty intervals.

∀c,ys:ys sorted by s∧(∀y∈ys: sc≤sy)∧sc<ec∧(∀y∈ys: sy<ey)⇒(∀i<j<∣g∣: egi<sgj)∧(∀o∈g: so<eo),g=go⁡(c,ys)\displaystyle \forall c, ys:\quad ys \text{ sorted by } s \land (\forall y \in ys:\ s_c \le s_y) \land s_c < e_c \land (\forall y \in ys:\ s_y < e_y) \Rightarrow \big(\forall i < j < |g|:\ e_{g_i} < s_{g_j}\big) \land \big(\forall o \in g:\ s_o < e_o\big), \quad g = \operatorname{go}(c, ys)
ParMetrics.mergeGo_withintheoremagreel.120

Every interval emitted by mergeGo lies in a window containing all inputs.

∀a,b,c,ys:a≤sc∧ec≤b∧(∀y∈ys: a≤sy∧ey≤b)⇒∀o∈go⁡(c,ys): a≤so∧eo≤b\displaystyle \forall a, b, c, ys:\quad a \le s_c \land e_c \le b \land (\forall y \in ys:\ a \le s_y \land e_y \le b) \Rightarrow \forall o \in \operatorname{go}(c, ys):\ a \le s_o \land e_o \le b
ParMetrics.mergeGo_covertheoremagreel.137

mergeGo covers exactly the points of its inputs.

∀c,ys,p:ys sorted by s∧(∀y∈ys: sc≤sy)⇒[(p∈c∨∃y∈ys: p∈y)  ⟺  ∃o∈go⁡(c,ys): p∈o]\displaystyle \forall c, ys, p:\quad ys \text{ sorted by } s \land (\forall y \in ys:\ s_c \le s_y) \Rightarrow \Big[\big(p \in c \lor \exists y \in ys:\ p \in y\big) \iff \exists o \in \operatorname{go}(c, ys):\ p \in o\Big]
ParMetrics.merge_disjoint_sortedtheoremagreel.166

**Merge is disjoint and sorted**: every merged interval ends before any later one starts, and every merged interval is non-empty (so they are also strictly sorted by start).

∀l, m=merge⁡(l):(∀i<j<∣m∣: emi<smj)∧(∀o∈m: so<eo)\displaystyle \forall l,\ m = \operatorname{merge}(l):\quad \big(\forall i < j < |m|:\ e_{m_i} < s_{m_j}\big) \land \big(\forall o \in m:\ s_o < e_o\big)
ParMetrics.merge_covertheoremagreel.186

**Merge keeps coverage**: a point is in some input interval iff it is in some merged interval.

∀l,p:(∃i∈l: si≤p<ei)  ⟺  (∃o∈merge⁡(l): so≤p<eo)\displaystyle \forall l, p:\quad (\exists i \in l:\ s_i \le p < e_i) \iff (\exists o \in \operatorname{merge}(l):\ s_o \le p < e_o)
ParMetrics.merge_withintheoremagreel.212

∀a,b,l:(∀i∈l: a≤si∧ei≤b)⇒∀o∈merge⁡(l): a≤so∧eo≤b\displaystyle \forall a, b, l:\quad (\forall i \in l:\ a \le s_i \land e_i \le b) \Rightarrow \forall o \in \operatorname{merge}(l):\ a \le s_o \land e_o \le b
ParMetrics.sum_len_letheoremagreel.245

Separated non-empty intervals inside [a,b][a, b] have total length at most b−ab - a.

ParMetrics.busy_le_alivetheoremagreel.262

**Busy time never exceeds the window** (an agent cannot be busy longer than it is alive).

∀a,b,l:busy⁡a,b(l)≤b−˙a\displaystyle \forall a, b, l:\quad \operatorname{busy}_{a,b}(l) \le b \mathbin{\dot-} a
ParMetrics.div_le_of_le_multheoremagreel.282

The rational quotient of two naturals is at most k when the numerator is at most k times the denominator.

∀x,y,k∈N:x≤k⋅y⇒x/y≤k in Q(x,y,k cast to Q; x/0=0)\displaystyle \forall x, y, k \in \mathbb N:\quad x \le k \cdot y \Rightarrow x / y \le k \text{ in } \mathbb{Q} \qquad (x, y, k \text{ cast to } \mathbb{Q};\ x / 0 = 0)
ParMetrics.busy_sum_letheoremagreel.301

∀a,b,ag:∑l∈agbusy⁡a,b(l)≤∣ag∣⋅(b−˙a)\displaystyle \forall a, b, \mathit{ag}:\quad \sum_{l \in \mathit{ag}} \operatorname{busy}_{a,b}(l) \le |\mathit{ag}| \cdot (b \mathbin{\dot-} a)

ParMetrics.segSum_letheoremagreel.363

Gap sums of a sorted list inside [a,b][a, b] are at most b−ab - a.

∀f,l,a,b:l sorted∧(∀p∈l: a≤p≤b)⇒segSum⁡f(l)≤b−˙a\displaystyle \forall f, l, a, b:\quad l \text{ sorted} \land (\forall p \in l:\ a \le p \le b) \Rightarrow \operatorname{segSum}_f(l) \le b \mathbin{\dot-} a
ParMetrics.serial_share_le_onetheoremagreel.385

**The serial share is at most 1.**

∀a,b,ag:serialShare⁡a,b(ag)≤1\displaystyle \forall a, b, \mathit{ag}:\quad \operatorname{serialShare}_{a,b}(\mathit{ag}) \le 1

Membership in preds.

ParMetrics.le_maxltheoremagreel.510

ParMetrics.weight_snoctheoremagreel.563

Weight of an extended path.

Path ends are nodes.

ParMetrics.kinv_inittheoremagreel.621

ParMetrics.kinv_steptheoremagreel.628

One step of Kahn's pass keeps the invariant.

∀n,w,E,D,R,v:KInv(D,R)∧v∈R∧preds⁡(v)⊆keys⁡(D)⇒KInv((v,wv+maxl⁡(look⁡(D,preds⁡(v))))::D, R∖{v})\displaystyle \forall n, w, E, D, R, v:\quad \mathrm{KInv}(D, R) \land v \in R \land \operatorname{preds}(v) \subseteq \operatorname{keys}(D) \Rightarrow \mathrm{KInv}\big((v, w_v + \operatorname{maxl}(\operatorname{look}(D, \operatorname{preds}(v)))) :: D,\ R \setminus \{v\}\big)
ParMetrics.kahn_sometheoremagreel.690

In a topologically ordered record with unique keys, everything that reaches a recorded node is recorded and differs from it.

replayFrom_totaltheoremagreel.859

The replay tally counts every event exactly once.

∀v,t,es:∣replay⁡(v,t,es)2∣=∣t∣+∣es∣\displaystyle \forall v, t, es:\quad |\operatorname{replay}(v, t, es)_2| = |t| + |es|
exec_spectheoremagreel.873

A command other than reset keeps the server indexed, and its console state is the fold of apply over the command's events.

∀v,c:Indexed⁡(v)∧c≠reset  ⇒  Indexed⁡(exec⁡(v,c)1)∧st⁡(exec⁡(v,c)1)=foldl⁡(apply⁡,st⁡(v),ev⁡(c))\displaystyle \forall v, c:\quad \operatorname{Indexed}(v) \land c \ne \mathrm{reset} \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{Indexed}(\operatorname{exec}(v, c)_1) \land \operatorname{st}(\operatorname{exec}(v, c)_1) = \operatorname{foldl}(\operatorname{apply}, \operatorname{st}(v), \operatorname{ev}(c))
run_eq_foldtheoremagreel.886

**Serve is the fold.** After any sequence of serve calls without a reset, the server is indexed and its console state is the left fold of apply over all their events, in order.

∀v,[c1,…,cn]:Indexed⁡(v)∧∀i, ci≠reset  ⇒  Indexed⁡(v′)∧st⁡(v′)=foldl⁡(apply⁡,st⁡(v),ev⁡(c1)+ ⁣ ⁣+⋯+ ⁣ ⁣+ev⁡(cn)),v′=run⁡(v,[c1,…,cn])\displaystyle \forall v, [c_1, \dots, c_n]:\quad \operatorname{Indexed}(v) \land \forall i,\ c_i \ne \mathrm{reset} \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{Indexed}(v') \land \operatorname{st}(v') = \operatorname{foldl}\big(\operatorname{apply}, \operatorname{st}(v), \operatorname{ev}(c_1) \mathbin{+\!\!+} \cdots \mathbin{+\!\!+} \operatorname{ev}(c_n)\big), \quad v' = \operatorname{run}(v, [c_1, \dots, c_n])
run_init_eq_projecttheoremagreel.900

From a fresh server, the console state after serve calls without a reset is the projection (full replay) of their events.

∀[c1,…,cn]:(∀i, ci≠reset)  ⇒  st⁡(run⁡(v0,[c1,…,cn]))=project⁡(ev⁡(c1)+ ⁣ ⁣+⋯+ ⁣ ⁣+ev⁡(cn))\displaystyle \forall [c_1, \dots, c_n]:\quad (\forall i,\ c_i \ne \mathrm{reset}) \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{st}(\operatorname{run}(v_0, [c_1, \dots, c_n])) = \operatorname{project}\big(\operatorname{ev}(c_1) \mathbin{+\!\!+} \cdots \mathbin{+\!\!+} \operatorname{ev}(c_n)\big)
apply_each_eq_replaytheoremagreel.909

Applying events one call at a time gives the same console state as one replay call, and both equal the projection of the events.

∀[e1,…,en]:st⁡(run⁡(v0,[apply(e1),…,apply(en)]))=st⁡(run⁡(v0,[replay([e1,…,en])]))=project⁡([e1,…,en])\displaystyle \forall [e_1, \dots, e_n]:\quad \operatorname{st}(\operatorname{run}(v_0, [\mathrm{apply}(e_1), \dots, \mathrm{apply}(e_n)])) = \operatorname{st}(\operatorname{run}(v_0, [\mathrm{replay}([e_1, \dots, e_n])])) = \operatorname{project}([e_1, \dots, e_n])
run_resettheoremagreel.927

A reset forgets everything before it: the calls after the last reset decide the state.

∀v,cs,rs:run⁡(v,cs+ ⁣ ⁣+reset::rs)=run⁡(v0,rs)\displaystyle \forall v, cs, rs:\quad \operatorname{run}(v, cs \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathrm{reset} :: rs) = \operatorname{run}(v_0, rs)
refused_unchangedtheoremagreel.934

A refused console.apply leaves the server state unchanged and reports no changed rows.

∀v,e,w,Δ:exec⁡(v,apply(e))2=applied(refused(w),Δ)  ⇒  exec⁡(v,apply(e))1=v  ∧  Δ=([ ],[ ],[ ])\displaystyle \forall v, e, w, \Delta:\quad \operatorname{exec}(v, \mathrm{apply}(e))_2 = \mathrm{applied}(\mathrm{refused}(w), \Delta) \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{exec}(v, \mathrm{apply}(e))_1 = v \;\land\; \Delta = ([\,], [\,], [\,])
accepted_changedtheoremagreel.946

An accepted fresh console.apply on an indexed server reports exactly the rows the event touched in the new console state.

∀v,e,Δ:Indexed⁡(v)∧exec⁡(v,apply(e))2=applied(accepted(false),Δ)  ⇒  Δ=touched⁡(st⁡(exec⁡(v,apply(e))1),e)\displaystyle \forall v, e, \Delta:\quad \operatorname{Indexed}(v) \land \operatorname{exec}(v, \mathrm{apply}(e))_2 = \mathrm{applied}(\mathrm{accepted}(\mathrm{false}), \Delta) \;\Rightarrow\; \Delta = \operatorname{touched}(\operatorname{st}(\operatorname{exec}(v, \mathrm{apply}(e))_1), e)
query_keepstheoremagreel.959

A query changes nothing and answers the board and the board plan of the current console state.

∀v,now,seq:exec⁡(v,query(now,seq))=(v, board(board⁡(st⁡(v),now,seq), Plan.view⁡(st⁡(v).plan)))\displaystyle \forall v, \mathit{now}, \mathit{seq}:\quad \operatorname{exec}(v, \mathrm{query}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{seq})) = \big(v,\ \mathrm{board}(\operatorname{board}(\operatorname{st}(v), \mathit{now}, \mathit{seq}),\ \operatorname{Plan.view}(\operatorname{st}(v).\mathit{plan}))\big)
query_eq_of_sttheoremagreel.967

The query reply is a function of the console state alone (not of the indexes or of how the state was reached).

∀v,w,now,seq:st⁡(v)=st⁡(w)  ⇒  exec⁡(v,query(now,seq))2=exec⁡(w,query(now,seq))2\displaystyle \forall v, w, \mathit{now}, \mathit{seq}:\quad \operatorname{st}(v) = \operatorname{st}(w) \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{exec}(v, \mathrm{query}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{seq}))_2 = \operatorname{exec}(w, \mathrm{query}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{seq}))_2
query_after_runtheoremagreel.976

After serve calls without a reset from a fresh server, the query reply is the board and the board plan of the projection of their events.

∀cs=[c1,…,cn],now,seq:(∀c∈cs, c≠reset)  ⇒  exec⁡(run⁡(v0,cs),query(now,seq))2=board(board⁡(σ,now,seq), Plan.view⁡(σ.plan)), σ=project⁡(ev⁡(c1)+ ⁣ ⁣+⋯+ ⁣ ⁣+ev⁡(cn))\displaystyle \forall cs = [c_1, \dots, c_n], \mathit{now}, \mathit{seq}:\quad (\forall c \in cs,\ c \ne \mathrm{reset}) \;\Rightarrow\; \operatorname{exec}(\operatorname{run}(v_0, cs), \mathrm{query}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{seq}))_2 = \mathrm{board}\big(\operatorname{board}(\sigma, \mathit{now}, \mathit{seq}),\ \operatorname{Plan.view}(\sigma.\mathit{plan})\big),\ \sigma = \operatorname{project}(\operatorname{ev}(c_1) \mathbin{+\!\!+} \cdots \mathbin{+\!\!+} \operatorname{ev}(c_n))

BreakpointFacts

Facts about the 30 breakpoint conditionsFw/Site/BreakpointFacts.lean · 55 theorems · 3 definitions · 58/58 reviewed
Breakpoints.catalogue_lengththeoremagreel.20

The catalogue has the inventory's 30 media conditions.

∣catalogue∣=30\displaystyle |\mathrm{catalogue}| = 30

There are exactly thirty conditions.

Breakpoints.catalogue_ids_noduptheoremagreel.27

Inventory ids and TS ids are pairwise distinct.

i≠j⇒idi≠idj∧tsi≠tsj\displaystyle i \ne j \Rightarrow \mathrm{id}_i \ne \mathrm{id}_j \land \mathrm{ts}_i \ne \mathrm{ts}_j

No two conditions share a name.

Breakpoints.catalogue_queries_noduptheoremagreel.34

No two catalogue entries are the same query.

i≠j⇒qi≠qj\displaystyle i \ne j \Rightarrow q_i \ne q_j

The thirty conditions are syntactically distinct.

Breakpoints.catalogue_csstheoremagreel.41

**Byte-exact CSS.** The printed normal form of every condition equals the inventory's condition string (breakpoints.json, schema fw.breakpoints/1, ids mq.*).

∀i<30. (idi,tsi,css(qi))=(idiinv,ti,siinv),t=(rmReduce,rmNopref,…,c1000Nodw)\displaystyle \forall i < 30.\ (\mathrm{id}_i, \mathrm{ts}_i, \mathrm{css}(q_i)) = (\mathrm{id}^{inv}_i, t_i, s^{inv}_i),\quad t = (\texttt{rmReduce}, \texttt{rmNopref}, \dots, \texttt{c1000Nodw})

where tt is the list of TS ids written in the theorem (breakpoints.json has no TS-id field).

Each condition prints exactly as the inventory writes it, under the listed TS id.

Breakpoints.catalogue_edgestheoremagreel.82

**Edges.** The tagged edges read off each condition's syntax equal the inventory's edges list (feature, lower pixel of the pair N | N+1).

∀i<30. E(qi)=Eiinv\displaystyle \forall i < 30.\ E(q_i) = E^{inv}_i

Every condition has exactly the edges the inventory lists, in the same order.

Breakpoints.MQ.eval_indep_height_dprtheoremagreel.385

Height, device height and DPR never change any condition.

∀q,e,h′,dh′,r′:⟦q⟧e[h:=h′, dh:=dh′, r:=r′]=⟦q⟧e\displaystyle \forall q, e, h', d_h', r':\quad \llbracket q \rrbracket_{e[h:=h',\,d_h:=d_h',\,r:=r']} = \llbracket q \rrbracket_e

The page has no height, device-height or resolution media query, so these inputs never change a media condition (height can still change layout through vh units and JS viewport-height reads).

Breakpoints.c860_le_c1000_le_c1030theoremagreel.404

The combos are nested: combo 860 implies combo 1000, which implies combo 1030.

e⊨C860⇒e⊨C1000∧e⊨C1000⇒e⊨C1030\displaystyle e \models C_{860} \Rightarrow e \models C_{1000} \quad\land\quad e \models C_{1000} \Rightarrow e \models C_{1030}

A wider combo matches wherever a narrower one does.

Breakpoints.c1000Nodw_vs_c1000theoremagreel.423

c1000Nodw implies c1000, and they differ exactly for a small screen, a viewport above 1000 px, and no matching touch arm.

(e⊨C1000nodw⇒e⊨C1000)∧(e⊨C1000∧e⊭C1000nodw  ⟺  dw≤500∧w>1000∧¬(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle (e \models C^{nodw}_{1000} \Rightarrow e \models C_{1000}) \land (e \models C_{1000} \land e \not\models C^{nodw}_{1000} \iff d_w \le 500 \land w > 1000 \land \neg(\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

The countdown's combo is the commission combo minus the device-width arm, and only that arm separates them.

Breakpoints.overlap_c860_wGe861theoremagreel.457

**Overlap C860 / >=861.** Both match exactly on a viewport of at least 861 px with a small screen or a touch input up to 1200 px.

e⊨C860∧e⊨(w≥861)  ⟺  w≥861∧(dw≤500∨(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle e \models C_{860} \land e \models (w \ge 861) \iff w \ge 861 \land (d_w \le 500 \lor (\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

A touch tablet at 861-1200 px or a phone in landscape takes both the compact and the desktop rules.

Breakpoints.overlap_c1000_wGe1001theoremagreel.477

**Overlap C1000 / >=1001.** Both match exactly on a viewport of at least 1001 px with a small screen or a touch input up to 1200 px.

e⊨C1000∧e⊨(w≥1001)  ⟺  w≥1001∧(dw≤500∨(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle e \models C_{1000} \land e \models (w \ge 1001) \iff w \ge 1001 \land (d_w \le 500 \lor (\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

Commission compact and the desktop platform mission title apply together on a touch tablet at 1001-1200 px.

Breakpoints.overlap_c1000_wGe1001Nopreftheoremagreel.497

**Overlap C1000 / >=1001 and no-preference.** As overlap_c1000_wGe1001, plus motion allowed.

e⊨C1000∧e⊨(w≥1001∧μ=no-preference)  ⟺  w≥1001∧μ=no-preference∧(dw≤500∨(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle e \models C_{1000} \land e \models (w \ge 1001 \land \mu = \text{no-preference}) \iff w \ge 1001 \land \mu = \text{no-preference} \land (d_w \le 500 \lor (\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

The sticky desktop commission and the compact commission both match on a touch tablet at 1001-1200 px with motion on.

Breakpoints.c860_not_wLe860theoremagreel.517

**Never mix pure 860 and C860.** C860 holds while (width<=860px) fails exactly above 860 px with a small screen or a touch input up to 1200 px.

e⊨C860∧e⊭(w≤860)  ⟺  w>860∧(dw≤500∨(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle e \models C_{860} \land e \not\models (w \le 860) \iff w > 860 \land (d_w \le 500 \lor (\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

Pure-width users take the desktop path where combo users take the compact path, so one cannot stand in for the other.

Breakpoints.wLe860_imp_c860theoremagreel.537

(width<=860px) implies C860 (the converse fails, see c860_not_wLe860).

e⊨(w≤860)⇒e⊨C860\displaystyle e \models (w \le 860) \Rightarrow e \models C_{860}

Breakpoints.deskDeck_ifftheoremagreel.554

The desktop deck runs exactly on a viewport of at least 861 px, a screen wider than 500 px, no touch arm, and motion allowed.

deskDeck(e)  ⟺  w≥861∧dw>500∧¬(touch(e)∧w≤1200)∧μ≠reduce\displaystyle \mathrm{deskDeck}(e) \iff w \ge 861 \land d_w > 500 \land \neg(\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200) \land \mu \ne \text{reduce}

Breakpoints.touchTablet_overlaptheoremagreel.578

touch(e)∧861≤w≤1200⇒e⊨C860∧e⊨(w≥861)∧¬deskDeck(e)\displaystyle \mathrm{touch}(e) \land 861 \le w \le 1200 \Rightarrow e \models C_{860} \land e \models (w \ge 861) \land \neg\mathrm{deskDeck}(e)

Breakpoints.smallScreen_overlaptheoremagreel.588

dw≤500∧w≥861⇒e⊨C860∧e⊨(w≥861)∧¬deskDeck(e)\displaystyle d_w \le 500 \land w \ge 861 \Rightarrow e \models C_{860} \land e \models (w \ge 861) \land \neg\mathrm{deskDeck}(e)

A phone in landscape takes both CSS paths and the compact JS deck.

Breakpoints.gap_ifftheoremagreel.610

**The gaps are real.** For every edge N, a width strictly between N and N+1 matches neither (width<=Npx) nor (width>=N+1px), and those are exactly the widths that match neither.

¬(w≤N)∧¬(w≥N+1)  ⟺  N<w<N+1,N<N+12<N+1\displaystyle \neg(w \le N) \land \neg(w \ge N{+}1) \iff N < w < N{+}1, \qquad N < N{+}\tfrac12 < N{+}1

Between the last pixel of a band and the first pixel of the next lies an open interval that neither side claims.

Breakpoints.no_gap_ofNattheoremagreel.622

At whole-pixel widths there is no gap: (width<=Npx) and (width>=N+1px) are complementary.

∀k∈N. k≤N  ⟺  ¬(k≥N+1)\displaystyle \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\ k \le N \iff \neg(k \ge N{+}1)

Integer probes can never land in a fractional gap.

Breakpoints.half_boundstheoremagreel.630

A length of value N+12N + \tfrac12 lies strictly between NN and N+1N+1, in any representation.

∀N,p,q∈N, q>0:2p=(2N+1) q⇒Nq<p∧p<(N+1) q\displaystyle \forall N, p, q \in \mathbb{N},\ q > 0:\quad 2p = (2N+1)\,q \Rightarrow N q < p \land p < (N+1)\,q

A half-pixel width is never a whole pixel and never reaches the next one.

Breakpoints.half_valuetheoremagreel.638

The probe Px.half N has value N+12N + \tfrac12 in the form the gap theorems take.

∀N∈N:2⋅num(half(N))=(2N+1)⋅den(half(N))\displaystyle \forall N \in \mathbb{N}:\quad 2 \cdot \mathrm{num}(\mathrm{half}(N)) = (2N+1) \cdot \mathrm{den}(\mathrm{half}(N))

Px.half N satisfies the hypothesis of gap600 … gap1000 for its N.

Breakpoints.gap600theoremagreel.646

Gap 600 at any width whose value is 600.5: <=600, 601-1279 and 601-1511 all fail, while >600 matches.

∀e. pwqw=12012 (i.e. 2pw=1201 qw)⇒e⊭(w≤600)∧e⊭(601≤w≤1279)∧e⊭(601≤w≤1511)∧e⊨(w>600)\displaystyle \forall e.\ \tfrac{p_w}{q_w} = \tfrac{1201}{2}\ (\text{i.e. } 2p_w = 1201\,q_w) \Rightarrow e \not\models (w \le 600) \land e \not\models (601 \le w \le 1279) \land e \not\models (601 \le w \le 1511) \land e \models (w > 600)

At 600.5 px (in any representation, e.g. Px.half 600 or 2402/4) the hero has neither its phone rules nor its 601+ orbit rules, but >600 rules apply.

Breakpoints.gap640theoremagreel.661

Gap 640 at any width whose value is 640.5: <=640 and 641-1000 fail, while >640 matches.

∀e. pwqw=12812 (i.e. 2pw=1281 qw)⇒e⊭(w≤640)∧e⊭(641≤w≤1000)∧e⊨(w>640)\displaystyle \forall e.\ \tfrac{p_w}{q_w} = \tfrac{1281}{2}\ (\text{i.e. } 2p_w = 1281\,q_w) \Rightarrow e \not\models (w \le 640) \land e \not\models (641 \le w \le 1000) \land e \models (w > 640)

At 640.5 px (in any representation) neither the phone geometry nor the commission tablet band applies, but the >640 nav background does.

Breakpoints.gap860theoremagreel.676

Gap 860 at any width whose value is 860.5: <=860, >=861, >=861 and no-preference and 861-1000 all fail.

∀e. pwqw=17212 (i.e. 2pw=1721 qw)⇒e⊭(w≤860)∧e⊭(w≥861)∧e⊭(w≥861∧μ=no-preference)∧e⊭(861≤w≤1000)\displaystyle \forall e.\ \tfrac{p_w}{q_w} = \tfrac{1721}{2}\ (\text{i.e. } 2p_w = 1721\,q_w) \Rightarrow e \not\models (w \le 860) \land e \not\models (w \ge 861) \land e \not\models (w \ge 861 \land \mu = \text{no-preference}) \land e \not\models (861 \le w \le 1000)

At 860.5 px (in any representation) neither the pure-width phone path nor the desktop path matches, in CSS and in JS.

Breakpoints.gap1000theoremagreel.692

Gap 1000 at any width whose value is 1000.5: <=1000, >=1001, >=1001 and no-preference, 641-1000 and 861-1000 all fail (the combos c1000 and c1000-nodw lose their (width<=1000px) arm).

∀e. pwqw=20012 (i.e. 2pw=2001 qw)⇒e⊭(w≤1000)∧e⊭(w≥1001)∧e⊭(w≥1001∧μ=no-preference)∧e⊭(641≤w≤1000)∧e⊭(861≤w≤1000)\displaystyle \forall e.\ \tfrac{p_w}{q_w} = \tfrac{2001}{2}\ (\text{i.e. } 2p_w = 2001\,q_w) \Rightarrow e \not\models (w \le 1000) \land e \not\models (w \ge 1001) \land e \not\models (w \ge 1001 \land \mu = \text{no-preference}) \land e \not\models (641 \le w \le 1000) \land e \not\models (861 \le w \le 1000)

At 1000.5 px (in any representation) none of the five rules (width<=1000px), (width>=1001px), (width>=1001px) and no-preference, 641-1000 and 861-1000 matches; the combos c1000 / c1000-nodw lose their (width<=1000px) arm but can still match through the device-width or touch arm.

checkCond(c,r)=[ ]  ⟺  r.id=c.id∧r.condition=css(q)∧r.kind=str(κ)∧r.features=features(q)∧r.edges=[(str(a),[N,N+1])](a,N)∈E(q)∧r.edges_px=edgesPx(q)∧((∃s∈r.equivalentForms. s starts with ()⇒legacy(q)≠⊥∧legacy(q)∈r.equivalentForms)\displaystyle \mathrm{checkCond}(c, r) = [\,] \iff r.\mathrm{id} = c.\mathrm{id} \land r.\mathrm{condition} = \mathrm{css}(q) \land r.\mathrm{kind} = \mathrm{str}(\kappa) \land r.\mathrm{features} = \mathrm{features}(q) \land r.\mathrm{edges} = [(\mathrm{str}(a), [N, N{+}1])]_{(a,N) \in E(q)} \land r.\mathrm{edges\_px} = \mathrm{edgesPx}(q) \land \big((\exists s \in r.\mathrm{equivalentForms}.\ s \text{ starts with } \texttt{(}) \Rightarrow \mathrm{legacy}(q) \ne \bot \land \mathrm{legacy}(q) \in r.\mathrm{equivalentForms}\big)

BreakpointGen.checkInventorydefagreel.167

Every mismatch between the Lean catalogue / matrix and the inventory document (empty when they agree).

checkInventory(I)=[ ]  ⟺  ∣R∣=30∧∀i<30. checkCond(ci,Ri)=[ ]∧I.edgePairs=[[N,N+1]]N∈widthEdgePairs∧I.deviceWidthPairs=[[500,501]]∧I.touch-rm.at=[[N,N+1]]N∈touchRmEdges∧I.estimate.loadsPerEngine=∣M∣∧∀(b,n)∈blockBreakdown. I.estimate.breakdown[b]=n\displaystyle \mathrm{checkInventory}(I) = [\,] \iff |R| = 30 \land \forall i < 30.\ \mathrm{checkCond}(c_i, R_i) = [\,] \land I.\mathrm{edgePairs} = [[N,N{+}1]]_{N \in \mathrm{widthEdgePairs}} \land I.\mathrm{deviceWidthPairs} = [[500,501]] \land I.\text{touch-rm.at} = [[N,N{+}1]]_{N \in \mathrm{touchRmEdges}} \land I.\mathrm{estimate.loadsPerEngine} = |M| \land \forall (b,n) \in \mathrm{blockBreakdown}.\ I.\mathrm{estimate.breakdown}[b] = n

Here RR is the list of I.conditions rows whose id starts with mq., in order, cic_i is the ii-th catalogue entry, and every I.* field other than conditions is read under I.matrix (touch-rm.at is the at field of the featureCombos.profiles entry with id touch-rm).

run exits 1 when --inventory is given and this list is not empty; opBreakpointsGen returns the list next to gen.

Command-line driver of lake exe breakgen [--inventory <breakpoints.json>] [--check <file>]: without --check it prints the generated JSON to stdout; with --check <file> it fails when the file's bytes differ from the generated text; with --inventory it first fails on any mismatch against the inventory.

run(args)={2--inventory P given∧P does not parse as JSON1--inventory P given∧checkInventory(IP)≠[ ]0else if --check f given∧bytes(f)=utf8(genText)1else if --check f given0, stdout:=genTextotherwise\displaystyle \mathrm{run}(\mathit{args}) = \begin{cases} 2 & \texttt{--inventory } P \text{ given} \land P \text{ does not parse as JSON} \\ 1 & \texttt{--inventory } P \text{ given} \land \mathrm{checkInventory}(I_P) \ne [\,] \\ 0 & \text{else if } \texttt{--check } f \text{ given} \land \mathrm{bytes}(f) = \mathrm{utf8}(\mathrm{genText}) \\ 1 & \text{else if } \texttt{--check } f \text{ given} \\ 0,\ \text{stdout} := \mathrm{genText} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

The breakpoint gate's test matrix, and the MUI-internal neutral queriesFw/Site/BreakpointMatrix.lean · 18 theorems · 21 definitions · 21/39 reviewed
Breakpoints.matrix_lengththeoremreview stalel.136

The matrix has 124 loads per engine.

∣M∣=124\displaystyle |M| = 124

One engine runs 124 page loads.

Breakpoints.matrix_blockstheoremreview stalel.143

Each block has exactly the inventory's number of loads, and there are no other blocks.

∀(b,n)∈breakdown. ∣{p∈M∣p.block=b}∣=n ∧ ∑n=∣M∣\displaystyle \forall (b, n) \in \mathrm{breakdown}.\ |\{p \in M \mid p.\mathrm{block} = b\}| = n \ \land\ \textstyle\sum n = |M|

The matrix matches matrix.estimate.breakdown block by block.

Breakpoints.matrix_ids_noduptheoremreview stalel.152

Probe ids are unique.

i≠j⇒id(pi)≠id(pj)\displaystyle i \ne j \Rightarrow \mathrm{id}(p_i) \ne \mathrm{id}(p_j)

Every load has its own name.

Breakpoints.matrix_edge_pairstheoremreview stalel.164

**Both sides of every edge, per required profile.** For the profiles desk, desk-rm, touch every one of the 15 width edges has probes at N and N+1; touch-rm has them at 600, 860, 1000, 1030, 1200; and dw-arm-isolate has screens 500 and 501 at each of the viewports 1001, 1031, 1201.

∀b∈{desk,desk-rm,touch} ∀N∈E15. ∃p,p′∈Mb. w(p)=N∧w(p′)=N+1,∀N∈Et. ∃p,p′∈Mtouch-rm. w(p)=N∧w(p′)=N+1,∀v∈{1001,1031,1201} ∀s∈{500,501}. ∃p∈Mdw. (w,dw)(p)=(v,s)\displaystyle \forall b \in \{\text{desk}, \text{desk-rm}, \text{touch}\}\ \forall N \in E_{15}.\ \exists p, p' \in M_b.\ w(p) = N \land w(p') = N{+}1, \quad \forall N \in E_{t}.\ \exists p, p' \in M_{\text{touch-rm}}.\ w(p) = N \land w(p') = N{+}1, \quad \forall v \in \{1001, 1031, 1201\}\ \forall s \in \{500, 501\}.\ \exists p \in M_{\text{dw}}.\ (w, d_w)(p) = (v, s)

The matrix hits both sides of every edge in every input mode the inventory requires.

Breakpoints.matrix_observes_every_edgetheoremreview stalel.196

**The matrix sees every edge flip.** For every one of the 30 conditions and every edge (axis, N) it lists, the matrix contains two probes of one block that agree on all discrete features, sit at N and N+1 on that axis, and give the condition different values.

∀i<30 ∀(a,N)∈E(qi) ∃p,p′∈M. blk(p)=blk(p′)∧p∼p′∧a(p)=N∧a(p′)=N+1∧⟦qi⟧p≠⟦qi⟧p′\displaystyle \forall i < 30\ \forall (a, N) \in E(q_i)\ \exists p, p' \in M.\ \mathrm{blk}(p) = \mathrm{blk}(p') \land p \sim p' \land a(p) = N \land a(p') = N{+}1 \land \llbracket q_i \rrbracket_p \ne \llbracket q_i \rrbracket_{p'}

Every listed edge is a real flip, and the matrix catches it; with MQ.eval_congr no other flip exists.

Breakpoints.matrix_pairs_agreetheoremreview stalel.208

**Desktop-profile pairs differ only in size.** In the desk, desk-rm, touch and touch-rm blocks, the probes at N and N+1 agree on every discrete feature.

∀b∈{desk,desk-rm,touch,touch-rm} ∀N∈E15 ∀p,p′∈Mb. w(p)=N∧w(p′)=N+1⇒p∼p′\displaystyle \forall b \in \{\text{desk}, \text{desk-rm}, \text{touch}, \text{touch-rm}\}\ \forall N \in E_{15}\ \forall p, p' \in M_b.\ w(p) = N \land w(p') = N{+}1 \Rightarrow p \sim p'

An edge pair varies the width (and the screen width that tracks it), nothing else a query reads.

Breakpoints.matrix_fractional_in_gapstheoremreview stalel.221

**Fractional probes land in the gaps, one per gap.** Listing, for each fractional-gaps probe in matrix order, the edges N among 600, 640, 860, 1000 with N < w < N+1 gives exactly [600], [640], [860], [1000]: there are four probes, each lies strictly inside exactly one gap, and the four gaps are distinct.

( [N←(600,640,860,1000)∣N<w(p)<N+1] )p∈Mfrac=([600],[640],[860],[1000])\displaystyle \big(\,[N \leftarrow (600, 640, 860, 1000) \mid N < w(p) < N{+}1]\,\big)_{p \in M_{\text{frac}}} = ([600], [640], [860], [1000])

The four fractional loads cover the four gaps at 600, 640, 860 and 1000, one load strictly inside each.

Breakpoints.Px.mulWhole_of_device_pxtheoremreview pendingl.253

A width that is a whole number PP of device pixels divided by the ratio rr has a whole product with rr.

∀x,r∈Px, ∀P∈N,x.num⋅r.num=P⋅(x.den⋅r.den)  ⟹  MulWhole(x,r)\displaystyle \forall x, r \in \mathrm{Px},\ \forall P \in \mathbb N,\quad x.\mathrm{num} \cdot r.\mathrm{num} = P \cdot (x.\mathrm{den} \cdot r.\mathrm{den}) \implies \mathrm{MulWhole}(x, r)

A Chromium media width P/rP / r (with PP whole physical px) always satisfies the realizability test.

Breakpoints.matrix_width_dpr_wholetheoremreview pendingl.263

**Realizability.** Every probe of the matrix asks for a whole number of device pixels across.

∀p∈M,MulWhole(w(p), r(p))\displaystyle \forall p \in M,\quad \mathrm{MulWhole}(w(p),\ r(p))

Every probe width times its DPR is whole; the fractional gaps run at DPR 2, (N+12)⋅2=2N+1(N + \tfrac12) \cdot 2 = 2N + 1.

Breakpoints.matrix_whole_ifftheoremreview pendingl.270

The probe widths are whole exactly outside the fractional-gaps block.

Breakpoints.fractional_dpr_indeptheoremreview pendingl.278

Moving a fractional probe from DPR 54\tfrac54 to DPR 2 changes no condition, so no expected vector changes.

∀N∈N, ∀q∈MQ,⟦q⟧desk(N+12, 900, 2, no-preference)=⟦q⟧desk(N+12, 900, 54, no-preference)\displaystyle \forall N \in \mathbb N,\ \forall q \in \mathrm{MQ},\quad \llbracket q \rrbracket_{\mathrm{desk}(N + \frac12,\ 900,\ 2,\ \text{no-preference})} = \llbracket q \rrbracket_{\mathrm{desk}(N + \frac12,\ 900,\ \frac54,\ \text{no-preference})}

**(b)** The two hover queries of the neutral set are exactly the inventory's hover conditions (mq.hover-hover, mq.hover-none), and inside the hover-pointer-cross block each takes both values at one viewport size.

nhh=qmq.hover-hover∧nhn=qmq.hover-none∧∀q∈{nhh,nhn} ∃p,p′∈Mcross. (w,h)(p)=(w,h)(p′)∧p⊨q∧p′⊭q\displaystyle n_{hh} = q_{\text{mq.hover-hover}} \land n_{hn} = q_{\text{mq.hover-none}} \land \forall q \in \{n_{hh}, n_{hn}\}\ \exists p, p' \in M_{\text{cross}}.\ (w,h)(p) = (w,h)(p') \land p \models q \land p' \not\models q

Breakpoints.matrix_dw_armtheoremreview stalel.395

The device-width arm alone: at viewports 1031 and 1201 with a fine pointer, screen 500 vs 501 flips c860, c1000, c1030 and never c1000Nodw; at viewport 1001 it flips c860 and c1000 while c1030 already holds by width.

∀p∈Mdw. p⊭C1000nodw∧(dw(p)=500⇒p⊨C860∧p⊨C1000∧p⊨C1030)∧(dw(p)≠500⇒p⊭C860∧p⊭C1000∧(p⊨C1030  ⟺  w(p)=1001))\displaystyle \forall p \in M_{\text{dw}}.\ p \not\models C^{nodw}_{1000} \land \big(d_w(p) = 500 \Rightarrow p \models C_{860} \land p \models C_{1000} \land p \models C_{1030}\big) \land \big(d_w(p) \ne 500 \Rightarrow p \not\models C_{860} \land p \not\models C_{1000} \land (p \models C_{1030} \iff w(p) = 1001)\big)

(structural equality of Px values, as in the Lean; the block's probes are the viewports 1001, 1031, 1201 at screens 500 and 501.)

Phone landscape (932×430 on a 430×932 screen, touch) is in the C860 / >=861 overlap for both motion settings, but **not** in the C1000 / >=1001 overlap: 932 < 1001, so only C1000 matches there. (As the inventory's phone-landscape.why states, the C1000 / >=1001 overlap needs a viewport of at least 1001 px with a small screen or touch; the touch probes at 1031 and 1200 and the dw-arm-isolate probes with screen 500 provide it.)

obs(q,a,N)  ⟺  ∃p,p′∈M. a(p)=N∧a(p′)=N+1∧blk(p)=blk(p′)∧p∼p′∧⟦q⟧p≠⟦q⟧p′\displaystyle \mathrm{obs}(q, a, N) \iff \exists p, p' \in M.\ a(p) = N \land a(p') = N{+}1 \land \mathrm{blk}(p) = \mathrm{blk}(p') \land p \sim p' \land \llbracket q \rrbracket_p \ne \llbracket q \rrbracket_{p'}

Breakpoints of the original homepage, as decidable predicatesFw/Site/Breakpoints.lean · 5 theorems · 80 definitions · 85/85 reviewed
Breakpoints.Feature.holds_congrtheoremagreel.612

A single feature keeps its value when no cut of it separates the two environments.

e∼e′∧(∀N∈Ew(f). SameSideN(w,w′))∧(∀N∈Ed(f). SameSideN(dw,dw′))⇒⟦f⟧e=⟦f⟧e′\displaystyle e \sim e' \land (\forall N \in E_w(f).\ \mathrm{SameSide}_N(w,w')) \land (\forall N \in E_d(f).\ \mathrm{SameSide}_N(d_w,d_w')) \Rightarrow \llbracket f\rrbracket_e = \llbracket f\rrbracket_{e'}

A feature can only flip across one of its own edges.

Breakpoints.MQ.eval_congrtheoremagreel.653

**Edge sufficiency (rational widths).** A query keeps its value between two environments that agree on the discrete features and are on the same side of every width edge and every device-width edge of the query.

e∼e′∧(∀N∈Ew(q). SameSideN(w,w′))∧(∀N∈Ed(q). SameSideN(dw,dw′))⇒⟦q⟧e=⟦q⟧e′\displaystyle e \sim e' \land (\forall N \in E_w(q).\ \mathrm{SameSide}_N(w,w')) \land (\forall N \in E_d(q).\ \mathrm{SameSide}_N(d_w,d_w')) \Rightarrow \llbracket q\rrbracket_e = \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e'}

The truth value of any condition changes only at the edges listed by its syntax.

Breakpoints.sameSide_ofNattheoremagreel.672

For whole-pixel widths, being on the same side of edge N is just comparing with N.

SameSideN(a/1,b/1)  ⟺  (a≤N⇔b≤N)(a,b∈N)\displaystyle \mathrm{SameSide}_N(a/1, b/1) \iff (a \le N \Leftrightarrow b \le N) \qquad (a, b \in \mathbb{N})

At integer widths the two cuts of an edge coincide, so the pair N | N+1 is the whole edge.

Breakpoints.MQ.eval_ofNat_congrtheoremagreel.681

**Edge sufficiency (whole pixels).** At integer widths and device widths, a query has the same value at any two sizes that compare the same way with every edge of the query; so between consecutive edges it is constant and probing N and N+1 at each edge N observes every change.

e∼e′∧(∀N∈Ew(q). a≤N⇔b≤N)∧(∀N∈Ed(q). c≤N⇔d≤N)⇒⟦q⟧e[w:=a, dw:=c]=⟦q⟧e′[w:=b, dw:=d](a,b,c,d∈N)\displaystyle e \sim e' \land (\forall N \in E_w(q).\ a \le N \Leftrightarrow b \le N) \land (\forall N \in E_d(q).\ c \le N \Leftrightarrow d \le N) \Rightarrow \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e[w:=a,\,d_w:=c]} = \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e'[w:=b,\,d_w:=d]} \qquad (a,b,c,d \in \mathbb{N})

Whole-pixel widths in the same band between edges give the same answer.

Breakpoints.MQ.eval_const_on_bandtheoremagreel.696

**Bands.** If no width edge N of q satisfies a ≤ N < b, then q has the same value at every whole-pixel width from a to b (device width and discrete features fixed).

(∀N∈Ew(q). ¬(a≤N<b))∧a≤x≤b⇒⟦q⟧e[w:=a]=⟦q⟧e[w:=x](a,b,x∈N)\displaystyle (\forall N \in E_w(q).\ \neg(a \le N < b)) \land a \le x \le b \Rightarrow \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e[w:=a]} = \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e[w:=x]} \qquad (a,b,x \in \mathbb{N})

Between two consecutive edges a condition is constant.

Roles are committed agent files in .claude/agents/, each with its model, effort, context cap and write paths; pnpm fw roster:check keeps this table equal to the files. Scripts and hooks take over v1's routing, polling and device chores.

Not written so far: engine-researcher, source-locator, ref-librarian, and experiment-owner (it arrives with M5). At most 10 subagents at once; spawn-guard will cap teammates at 5 (it logs only until the user's three conditions hold, Q31). The real limit is this Mac's 16 GB of RAM, and counts now run on CI. Fable is used per call only, behind an ask rule; the lead asks it when it cannot decide a team problem.

The only inputs agents have: typed, refusable commands

WhoCommands (each one event; the Lean reducer accepts or refuses it)
the userstep answer or cancel; proposal decision; priority list; session booking; decision answer; best-build pick; thread posts and "answered"; math:sign
leadcard approve; fw land (refused unless the card is land-ready); card drop with a reason; rulings; queue move with a reason
ownercard open; park until a typed condition; wait on an agent; ask the lead; hand-back result (landed, no-gain, refuted, blocked); a note of ≤ 200 characters the reducer never reads

math-reviewerfw math:sign <decl>
any agentscreen, gate, run and device job requests; console-api runs the job and records the result

Coordination rules from the chat history

  • No recurring AI check prompts: scripts watch instead. fw watch computes team health in Lean (5 agent states, 14 alert codes) and wakes the lead only on an alert; the device watcher and a notice coalescer do the rest.
  • Nobody writes status: fw land --task <id> writes a Task: trailer, and the trailer marks the work-graph task done.
  • The lead watches for work that runs long against its estimate, and moves load-heavy work to CI (the mutation pass drove the Mac's load to about 500).
  • Kill only processes your own run started; pkill and killall are denied after an agent closed the user's browser.
  • Workers send results to their consumer; the lead gets ≤ 300 characters and a file path.
  • Agents cannot write console state: a strict sandbox and deny rules guard the gitignored .fw-console/, and console-api is its only writer.
  • Agent caches last 5 minutes (measured), so an agent idle longer with over 30k tokens of context is stopped and a fresh one starts from its handoff note.
  • After every compaction a hook will re-inject the roster, names and the lead's address (planned).
  • One plain command per Bash call; multi-step work is a committed pnpm fw command.
  • main moves only through the lead's fw land (ff-only); any other move shows up as a violation on the user's needs-you list.

Budget: looser, by the user's choice

Speed over token savings. No hard caps or stop rules: cost is reported daily against a forecast, with soft alerts for a milestone above 1.5× its forecast, a day above 2× the running average, or a cold-wake share above 10%. The one real stop is the provider's weekly usage limit, alerted at 60% and 80%.

Forecast ≈ $5,730 at list price, expected to run 20–40% higher with more Opus and concurrency; Lean-first adds about $700–1,100 of Lean work in place of $280 (both estimates).

reported per day: tokens by role · cache-read share · cold wakes · compactions · list-price $

A dependency graph, not a calendar

Roadmap

There are no dates. A workstream starts as soon as its inputs exist; independent ones run in parallel, each in its own worktree. Milestones M0–M6 are gates: conditions that must hold, not days. Time is measured, not planned: git history is the timeline, and the meter reports time and cost per gate. The live task list is docs/team/work-graph.json (tasks with dependencies, milestones, files and devices; status derived); the table below is the plan's view of it, with what has landed.

Public CI: where counts are measured

Chromium counts, WebKit Simulator counts, the breakpoint gate and WKTR run on GitHub Actions (the user's direction, 417d90d), with read-only contents, actions pinned by SHA and inputs passed through env. A workflow runs only when its inputs change, and a newer push cancels a stale run: before that, 21 of 28 runs touched no input and 248 of 414 job-minutes were wasted. The free plan allows 20 jobs at once, 5 of them macOS. This Mac keeps the phone sessions and one short debug run per harness change; a local run is never reported as a result. Agents may push only ci/* branches.

breakpoint-gate8 shards; 4 min 40 s on the first pass, 5 min 06 s on the third.

Review

Decisions

Everything the user decided on 2026-10-17 is applied. Revision 7 records the answers to Q1 (sessions), Q31 and Q33. Still open: Q32 from revision 6, and Q34 and Q35, two CSS questions for M2. Each open question shows the plan's recommendation; nothing is decided until the user answers.

QuestionStatusAnswer
Q32 A/B bench windowopenThe parallel-work bench (8 blocks, a random labeling out of 70) must run with no agent alive: about 96 minutes plus baselines. Recommended: one evening slot after M0, when no phone session is running.
Q34 MUI cssVariablesopenTurn on MUI's CSS-variables theme for the ported parts? It adds custom properties the original does not have. Recommended: off, so the style-work bound N4 stays within ±10 %.
Q35 Dead CSSopenAdd the original's unused CSS back as an inert sheet, so the rule count matches? Recommended: no; record the difference as a fixture parameter instead.
Q1 Phone sessionsdecidedOn demand: the user starts a session when an agent asks for one; no fixed windows. The second iPhone stays a free-play device, kept out of measurement.
Q31 Spawn-guarddecidedYes, switch to blocking, after three conditions: a liveness feed fills its alive/recent lists, one day of logs shows no wrong refusal, and the A/B bench has run (task spawn-enforce).
Q33 Unreachable breakpoint cellsdecidedA Simulator or device check for both the fractional gaps and the hover × pointer cross. The Lean gate gets an unreachable state, so such a cell can never pass silently.
Measure on CIdecidedChromium counts, WebKit Simulator counts, the breakpoint gate and WKTR run on GitHub Actions; this Mac keeps the phone sessions and short debug runs (417d90d).
Count classes (SPK-i)decidedDeterministic types compare frame by frame; stable types only as totals with margin 2t; quarantined types are never used. A type's class is the worst over at least 3 CI runs (6b4237e).
WKTRdecidedWebKit's prebuilt iOS-simulator build on GitHub's macos-26 runners first; a rented cloud Mac only if that fails (591a815).
Kill by namedecidedpkill and killall are denied for agents after one closed the user's browser; kill only your own PIDs (b205acc).
Q1 DevicesdecidediPhone 15 Pro Max on iOS 27.0.1 with Safari 27; Developer Mode allowed; no Android phone. The iOS 27.0 Simulator is installed to match; the Android emulator gives counts only.
Q2 Install LeandecidedYes. elan 4.2.4 from Homebrew's elan-init, Lean 4.35.0.
Q3 Repo visibilitydecidedPublic, MIT for our own code (changed from Private on 2026-10-17). Fastwork approved publishing its compiled site, fonts included; it enters git only as the unmodified snapshot. The no-copy rules still apply to our code.
Q4 MUI scopedecidedMUI everywhere, with Emotion AOT on MUI 9.5; Base UI per part and Pigment on MUI 9.0.1 as fallbacks.
Q12 Lean scopedecidedLean-first, by milestone; mutants and a per-module demotion rule replace the M4 go/no-go.
Q16 BudgetdecidedLooser: speed first; costs reported with soft alerts, no hard stops.
Q22 SandboxdecidedYes, strict, for every agent; no unsandboxed retry.
Q23 Console locationdecidedInside the repo in the gitignored .fw-console/, written only by console-api. main stays a normal branch; a move outside fw land is flagged.
Q24 Lean firstdecidedEverything reproducible in the console, site, measurement and tooling is specified and proved in Lean before coding; Lean runs it, generates it, or provides golden vectors. fwcore is the console brain.
BreakpointsdecidedEvery breakpoint of the original, identically, for every part: generated list, lint, gate before promotion.
Console upkeepdecidedNobody writes status; every view is derived from the event log.
Reading proofsdecidedMath, not Lean: docstring math, a generated math view, a build gate, a math-reviewer role.
Lean packagingdecidedMathlib-free core; optional FwMath package for proofs that need Mathlib.
InstallsdecidedHomebrew whenever a formula or cask exists; otherwise ask the lead first.

Defaults Q25–Q30, used unless the user objects

DefaultWhat it means
Q25 Math viewA tab in console-web, also openable alone; math on every theorem and every definition the user reads.
Q26 Lease starvationNo renewing while someone waits, plus a cap on total hold time, with a bounded-wait theorem.
Q27 Aging stepA tighter bound than one level per 300 s: every job starts within 2 h of a booked window that fits it.

Earlier defaults the plan uses unless the user objects
  • Q5: look and work parity for experiment parts, look parity for the rest, every breakpoint for all parts; a time box per part.
  • Q6: the parity reference is snapshot b1789284481295-a455e793; v1's best build becomes the v1-best preset.
  • Q7: expect 5–10 phone sessions before the first licensed class, started on demand; classes X and P always use the phone.
  • Q8: Chromium is a development aid with no fitted coefficients.
  • Q9: acceptance bands V-a to V-t; a licence is per change class.
  • Q10: no "less work" landing for style-affecting changes in WebKit until a test-runner element count (WKTR) exists. WKTR runs from WebKit's prebuilt products (about 315 MB) on GitHub's macos-26 runners; the rented cloud Mac is a fallback only.
  • Q11: optimized variants pass a compositor gate; 60 Hz is the canonical rate.
  • Q13: landing verdict 4 vs 4 runs, false-win rate at most 1/70 (proved in rev 6); 5 vs 5 (at most 1/252) or sequential when more than 3 comparisons.
  • Q14: question → build → screen → review → (device) → land, with classes W, SM, X, P.
  • Q15, Q19: raw traces and phone-screen recordings stay local.
  • Q17, Q18, Q20: one decision record on team operation after the M0 spikes; agent caches last 5 minutes (measured), so an agent idle longer is stopped and respawned from its handoff note, and never resumed over 250k tokens; no recurring AI check prompts.
  • Q21: SPK-r decides; Base UI per part first, Pigment for the whole site only if AOT fails at the mechanism level.
